brief.summary: Equities drifted lower, long-end Treasury yields rose to multi-decade highs, crude jumped on Iran/Houthi escalation, and credit spreads widened. The front end was described as anchored near 4%, while the 10-year around 5.33% and 30-year around 5.71% kept pressure on risk assets. Fed commentary stressed flexibility and a possible October skip, but guests debated whether the Fed must hike several more times; no explicit market odds were given. The dominant narrative was a capital-market squeeze: AI/hyperscaler borrowing competes with heavy Treasury supply while oil adds inflation risk. Tone was cautious/risk-off, though AI earnings and labor data remained resilient.
notable_quotes: There clearly is a problem with the sovereign bond market, pushback coming from investors, and yet the corporate bond market remains completely open.
We are starting to see the bite of higher rates, the volatility of the market, and the pace of the rise.
